# Summary of Cairn System Rules

## Pulses
A pulse is a growth mechanic where a cairn's height increases based on its current size. The increase equals the stride value plus the number of complete strides that fit into the current height. For example, a 20-mark cairn with stride 6 grows by 6 + 3 = 9 marks (since three full strides of 6 fit into 20), reaching 29 marks.

When applying multiple pulses in sequence, each pulse operates on the new height created by the previous pulse, not the original height. The stride count recalculates each time based on where the cairn stands.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks after a pulse happens. The amount lost equals the pulsed height divided by the leak size (rounded down). Leaks only apply to the height that resulted from the pulse, creating a net growth that's smaller than the pulse alone would suggest.

## Drains
Drains work in cycles: pulse, then lose a fixed number of marks. Unlike leaks, the drain amount never changes. A cairn eventually empties when the drain exceeds what pulses can add, though predicting exactly when requires calculating each cycle individually since pulse strength decreases as height decreases.

## Origins (Working Backwards)
You can reverse-engineer a starting height by undoing pulses. Work backwards one pulse at a time, solving for what height would have pulsed to create the current height. This process repeats for each pulse level.

## Merging
Two cairns combine into one using proportional shares (in tenths) plus a tether value. Tether is a multiplier based on the shorter cairn's "marks per ten" (height divided by 10, rounded down). Different tethers produce different results even with identical cairns and shares.
